segments: [he did not] wish to go out to fight with them.
Then zeal seized Leo the Patrician,
and he went out, fought, and defeated the Bulgars,
and killed their king.
And he entered, seized Michael,
shaved his head,
placed him in a monastery,
and castrated his sons.
And he reigned for seven and a half years.
And he made peace with the Bulgars,
giving them the salt marsh over which they had been fighting.
And in the year one thousand one hundred and twenty-five [of the Greeks, 813/814 AD], {OCR?}
[Nasir seized] Kayshum. {OCR?}
And Abu Shaykh built the walls of Edessa at the expense of the Edessenes.
Then Abdallah son of Hisham (Hashim) seized Harran,
and Umar seized Tella,
and Habib seized Resh'aina,
and Abdallah seized Marde,
and Abbas seized Cyrrhus [and] Sarug,
and Uthman seized Qinnasrin, Antioch, and Apamea.
And Thabit set up gates between the defiles (clisurae?) of Cilicia,
and stationed guards,
so that the region of Cilicia might become a harbor of refuge for the persecuted and the poor.
And Husayn the general, when plotting rebellion against the king Amin, said to the Persians:
"Amin is an aider of the Arabs and a hater of the Persians."
And he made a faction of them,
and they attacked Amin,
put irons on him, and imprisoned him.
And Husayn went out and sat upon the bridge of Baghdad,
and called to the armies to submit to Ma'mun.
Amin, however, sent oaths from prison to Husayn,
that only his life and his personal property should be granted to him.
And Husayn and the Persians, being grieved,
released him and seated him upon his throne.
And he swore to Husayn that he would not reckon against him the foolish deed,
and even gave him his signet-ring.
Husayn, however, did not believe it,
but fled to Harthama, the general of Ma'mun.
And Nasir the rebel gathered all the Qaysite Arabs, and they came to Callinicus,
and lodged in the courtyards of the Christians,
oppressing them with the burdens of expenses.
And they pressed al-Rafiqa with war.
And Patriarch Cyriacus and Theodosius of Edessa were present in it,
and from hunger they ate bread of rice and pulse.
And afterwards they made an uneasy peace,
with the Aqulaye [Kufans] ruling over Callinicus and the Persians over al-Rafiqa.
